Received Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Post-transplant monitoring in male recipient with female donor
Clinical History: AML post allogeneic stem cell transplant
Transplant Date: [redacted date]
Donor: Female

TEST PERFORMED
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis
Probes: CEP X (DXZ1) SpectrumOrange / CEP Y (DYZ3) SpectrumGreen
Manufacturer: Abbott Molecular

METHODOLOGY
FISH analysis was performed on interphase nuclei from peripheral blood using X and Y chromosome enumeration probes. A minimum of 200 interphase nuclei were scored for the presence of X and Y chromosome signals.

RESULTS
X chromosome signals: 200/200 cells (100%)
Y chromosome signals: 8/200 cells (4%)

INTERPRETATION
FISH analysis demonstrates 96% XX cells (donor-derived) and 4% XY cells (recipient-derived) in this male patient who received an allogeneic stem cell transplant from a female donor. This finding indicates >95% donor chimerism, which is consistent with successful engraftment.

The presence of 4% XY cells represents residual recipient cells. While high donor chimerism is favorable for engraftment status, it does not exclude the possibility of minimal residual disease.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Continue routine chimerism monitoring as per transplant protocol
2. Consider molecular disease marker monitoring if available for assessment of minimal residual disease
3. Correlation with morphologic and flow cytometric findings is recommended
4. Follow-up chimerism analysis in 1-2 months or as clinically indicated

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
